Pursuant to State and County Directives, San Gabriel City Hall is closed to the public and physical access
to the meeting has been suspended. To provide members of the public access to the meeting and an
opportunity to comment on items on and off the Agenda, the following opportunities have been
established:

Public Comments

Please email all public comments to cityclerk@sgch.org and include the following on the subject line of
your email: the section (Public Comment, Consent, Public Hearing, Continued Business, New Business) and
Item Number you are commenting on. The Clerk will read public comments into the record for up to the
three-minute limit. Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and

  Tuesday, March 2, 2021

    CALL TO ORDER
    PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Councilmember Ding
    ROLL CALL: Mayor Menchaca, Vice Mayor Liao, Council Members Ding,
  Harrington, Pu

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  2. PRESENTATION

  A. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of February 16, 2021.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of February 16, 2021.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are
  presented to the City Council for review and approval.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. SAFE, CLEAN WATER PROGRAM (MEASURE W) APPROPRIATION OF
  FUNDS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 2, 2021  2
   Los Angeles County voters approved the Safe, Clean Water (SCW) Program
  (Measure W) on November 6, 2018. It imposes a new parcel tax of 2.5 cents
  per square foot of impermeable area except as exempted. The tax revenue is
  allocated 10% to the Flood Control District (Los Angeles County Board of
  Supervisors) for administration, 40% directly to each respective municipality
  within Los Angeles County, and the remaining 50% to fund projects and
  programs under the SCW Program.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-13
  appropriating $180,000 in the Stormwater Fund.

  D. GENERAL PLAN HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT FOR
  THE 2020 CALENDAR YEAR

  As required by Government Code Section 65400(b), the Planning Division is
  required to provide an annual report to the California Department of Housing
  and Community Development (HCD) and to the Governor’s Office of Planning
  and Research (OPR) regarding the implementation of the General Plan’s
  Housing Element and how the City is meeting the regional housing needs for
  the community. The General Plan Annual Progress Report (APR) is an
  important tool to facilitate the implementation of the Housing Element and
  in tracking and monitoring the City’s progress in addressing the regional
  housing needs allocation (RHNA), including the number of housing units
  permitted by income level, the status of programs in the Housing Element,
  and efforts to remove governmental constraints.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the information
  contained in this staff report and direct staff to submit the housing report to
  the State Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD).

  E. LETTER TO OPPOSE UNLESS AMENDED SENATE BILL (SB) 9 (ATKINS) –
  INCREASED DENSITY IN SINGLE-FAMILY ZONES

  Following the action alert recently received from the League of California
  Cities, staff has prepared a Letter to Oppose Unless Amended SB 9 (Atkins)
  Increased Density in Single-Family Residential Zones. This bill would require
  a local government to ministerially approve a housing development
  containing two residential units in single-family residential zones and also

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 2, 2021  3
   require local governments to ministerially approve urban lot splits. In the
  Letter to Oppose Unless Amended, staff is proposing several amendments in
  order to address the City’s concerns of SB 9 as written.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Mayor or City Manager
  to sign the Letter to Oppose Unless Amended, and staff will send the signed
  position letter to the bill’s author, the City’s legislative representatives, the
  League of California Cities, and other stakeholders as deemed appropriate.

  F. PERMANENT LOCAL HOUSING ALLOCATION (PLHA) PROGRAM FUND
  ALLOCATION AND AMENDMENT TO EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATING
  AGREEMENT (ENA) WITH RELATED COMPANIES OF CALIFORNIA

  On October 6, 2020, City Council elected to utilize the City’s Permanent Local
  Housing Allocation (PLHA) funds toward the predevelopment, development,
  acquisition, rehabilitation, and preservation of multifamily, residential live-
  work, rental housing for low income households. These funds can be used
  toward the investigative work taking place at 405 South Del Mar Avenue
  during the current due diligence period as the City is in escrow to purchase
  the property in partnership with the Related Companies of California.
  Additionally, the City and Related Companies of California together intend to
  amend the Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (ENA) as it relates to the
  financial responsibilities of the parties, on this affordable housing project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council take the following actions:

  1. Allocate $23,982 of the Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) funds
  toward the ATLA survey and Phase I environmental study for 405 South
  Del Mar Avenue;
  2. Approve Amendment to the Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (ENA) with
  the Related Companies of California; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute any grant-related documentation.

  G. PROPOSITION 68  GRANT  –  PLAN  SUBMITTAL  AND  PARK
  IMPROVEMENTS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – March 2, 2021  4
   As presented at the October 20, 2020 City Council Meeting, the City of San
  Gabriel is submitting an application for grant funds through Statewide Park
  Development and Community Revitalization Program – Round 4, funded
  through Proposition 68. With this final round of funding, the state will award
  over $395 million in competitive grants for the creation of new and renovated
  parks and recreation opportunities in the most critically-underserved
  communities across California. The City will submit an application by the
  March 12, 2021 deadline for the renovation of Smith Park.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Review the proposed park layout to be submitted as part of the grant
  application; and
  2. Recommend that staff present the proposed funding sources and
  program fee changes at a future date, should the project be funded.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS – None.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members
  to report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, March 16, 2021,
  at 6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will
  be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website
  at www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF MARCH 2, 2021
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

CALL TO ORDER

Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
6:32 P.M. on Tuesday, March 2, 2021, with all Council Members and staff participating by
teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Ding.

ROLL CALL

Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
Council Members Absent:  None.
Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City
  Manager/Community Development Director Arminé
  Chaparyan, City Attorney Keith Lemieux, Community
  Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Rebecca
  Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris, Chief City Clerk
  Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Finance Director William Kaholokula, and Assistant City
  Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Menchaca announced the agenda order was approved.
2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  The presentation was made by Fire Chief Wallace and Police Chief Harris.

3. PUBLIC COMMENT – None.

4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Regarding Item 4G, Proposition 68 Grant – Plan Submittal and Park Improvements, in
  response to Council questions, staff clarified that the pool and building will be moved
  and enlarged; the new building will have individual shower stalls and dressing areas,

CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 4  March 2, 2021
   and separate restrooms for adults and youth; and use of Measure W funding would
  not help in qualifying for the grant.

  A motion was made by Council Member Pu, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to approve
  Consent Calendar Items 4A– 4G as presented.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A– 4G as presented by a vote of 5-0 as
  follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved:

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of February 16, 2021.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of February 16, 2021.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved the February 5, 2021, and February 11, 2021, Registers
  of Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. SAFE, CLEAN WATER PROGRAM (MEASURE W) APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 21-13 appropriating $180,000 in the
  Stormwater Fund.

  D. GENERAL PLAN HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT FOR THE
  2020 CALENDAR YEAR

  The City Council received and filed the information and direct staffed to submit the
  housing report to the State Department of Housing and Community Development
  (HCD).

  E. LETTER TO OPPOSE UNLESS AMENDED SENATE BILL (SB) 9 (ATKINS) –
  INCREASED DENSITY IN SINGLE-FAMILY ZONES

  The City Council authorized the Mayor or City Manager to sign the Letter to
  Oppose Unless Amended, and directed staff to send the signed position letter to
  the bill’s author, the City’s legislative representatives, the League of California
  Cities, and other stakeholders as deemed appropriate.

  F. PERMANENT LOCAL HOUSING ALLOCATION (PLHA) PROGRAM FUND
  ALLOCATION AND AMENDMENT TO EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATING AGREEMENT
  (ENA) WITH RELATED COMPANIES OF CALIFORNIA

  The City Council:

  1. Allocated $23,982 of the Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) funds
  toward the ATLA survey and Phase I environmental study for 405 South Del Mar
  Avenue;
  2. Approved the Amendment to the Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (ENA) with
  the Related Companies of California; and
CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 4  March 2, 2021
   3. Authorized the City Manager to execute any grant-related documentation.

  G. PROPOSITION 68 GRANT – PLAN SUBMITTAL AND PARK IMPROVEMENTS

  The City Council:

  1. Reviewed the proposed park layout to be submitted as part of the grant
  application; and
  2. Recommended that staff present the proposed funding sources and program
  fee changes at a future date, should the project be funded.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS – None.
 8. PUBLIC COMMENT – None.

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto expressed gratitude to Herald Christian Health Center and
  Community Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Perez for their facilitation of
  COVID-19 vaccinations for the community.

10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Liao reported on the Independent Cities Association conference, and the
  Hope Lions Club Walk for Health and other health activities.

  Council Member Pu expressed appreciation to the Herald Christian Health Center, City
  staff, CORE Response, and nursing students from Azusa Pacific University, Western
  University and West Coast University for their work in providing vaccinations; and
  reminded all to follow safety protocols for COVID-19.

  Council Member Ding thanked Herald Christian Health Center and volunteers for
  providing vaccines and commented on the need for bilingual help, and reported on
  the Hope Lions Club Walk for Health and K-9 fundraising.

  Mayor Menchaca applauded Herald Christian Health Center for their collaborative
  work with the City and San Gabriel Unified School District on vaccinations;
  commended Community Services/Interim Mission Playhouse Director Perez and staff
  for helping with vaccinations; announced that the application period for City
  commissions is open; and provided information on 2021 Outstanding Older American
  nominations.

11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

12. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Menchaca adjourned the meeting at 7:20 P.M.
